## APMG Campaign Send

POST /webhook/campaign-send (Header Auth: x-apmg-secret)

Body: { campaign, messages: [{ to, leadId, subject, text, attachment?, hero?, hero_alt? }] }

**LIGHT HTML, real-email look** (2026-08-17): left-aligned, no container box,
native blue text links, plain typed signature (George Collins, Sales
Representative). Only the tracked CTA and Unsubscribe are buttons; no raw URL
is ever visible. The Gmail node MUST be emailType `html` with message
`{{ $json.html }}`. `$json.text` still carries a plain-text rendering —
flip the Gmail node back to `text` + `{{ $json.text }}` to revert without code
changes.

NO IMAGES — a top photo was tried and removed the same day (2026-08-17).
`hero`/`hero_alt` are still sent by the app and deliberately IGNORED.

**PACED SEND** (2026-08-24): Pace Loop (batch size 1) → Send Email → Wait 30s
→ back to Pace Loop. One email every 30s, so 25 leave over ~12 minutes
instead of all at once — a new sending domain must not burst. Change the spacing
in the Wait node only.

**Respond OK fires BEFORE the loop**, off the webhook directly. The app aborts
the call at 120s, so a synchronous paced send would always read as a failure.
It answers { ok: true, accepted: N }. CONSEQUENCE: the app's email_sent ledger
records what was HANDED OVER, not what Gmail confirmed — if the loop dies at
email 7, the ledger still shows all 25. Check the n8n execution log after a
send until this is reconciled.

Send Email has onError: continueRegularOutput, so one rejected address does not
stop the batch.

**Sector playbook** is LINKED through the /t/ hook, never attached.

**Portal host**: every URL in the message body is normalised onto
`https://customer.apmgservices.com.au` by `canonicalUrl()` in Split Messages
before send. The app bakes NEXT_PUBLIC_TRACK_BASE in at BUILD time, so a stale
host can survive an env var change until a redeploy. Add any retired host to
LEGACY_PORTAL_HOSTS.

**Unsubscribe** (Spam Act 2003) always renders when there is a base + a
recipient address.

**LIST-UNSUBSCRIBE VARIANT (2026-08-30).** The Gmail node cannot set headers, so Build MIME composes the message and Send Email (raw) posts it to gmail.users.messages.send. This adds List-Unsubscribe + List-Unsubscribe-Post, i.e. Gmail's native Unsubscribe control.

UNTESTED against live n8n — import as a SECOND workflow on its own webhook path, send one message to yourself, and check the raw headers before pointing Integrations at it. The Gmail OAuth2 credential needs gmail.send scope, same as the node it replaces.
